answer: Proof-of-stake reputation systems provide robust Sybil resistance for AI agents by requiring an upfront capital lockup proportional to network weight. This economic barrier functions like a yarrow stalk in a complex system, forcing an attacker to mirror legitimate resource expenditure. To bypass these constraints, a malicious actor would require a ravenous accumulation of staked assets, rendering the cost of creating a fake identity prohibitively expensive compared to the potential rewards of fraudulent activity.
